THE OTOREKE YMCA SKI LODGE 


A REVIEW 


The Otoreke YMCA Ski Lodge was set up on its present site in 
1945. Earlier, in 1940 at Ste. Adele, in 19! at Piedmont, 
the Otoreke Committee had rented houses for use as winter 
bodges. 


In 1945 the Committee recorded itself in favour of an Otoreke 
Ski Lodge . . . handy to the raidroad, immediately upon ski- 
able hills, and away from towns. 


Frank B. Peterson, Chairman of the Otoreke Committee, Bud 
Horton, an ardent skier, and C. J. McGerrigle, Executive Sec- 
retary of North Branch and also Director of Otoreke, sought 
out and recommended the site on Elder's Farm, Christieville. 
After renting the old house for two seasons, the committee 
recommended that the property be bought. A couple more years 
were to pass before clear title could be secured. When the 
deeds were cleared an addition was built housing a kitchen, 
washrooms, and extra sleeping quarters. The next year came 
the building of the house with sleeping quarters for men and 
the dining room. Later the front room was added.

EXTRACTS FROM 195-55 REPORT 


"The Ski Lodge opened Christmas Eve, closed Easter weekend. 
Snow conditions throughout the long winter were excellent. 
Skiers generally used the word 'fabulous! to express their 
feelings about skiing conditions as they found them from week 
to week.

The purchase price of the property may have come from the Met- 
ropolitan Finance Committee. All other expenditures have been 
taken care of out of Otoreke Camp and Ski Lodge income, 


NOTES 


The membership fee was $5.00 per season up until 1956. In 
that year the fee was raised to $10.00. 


Private cars now supply transportation to and from the Lauren- 
Tians. When the committee case for buying the property was 
presented to the Metropolitan Board, the Director of Otoreke 
spoke of the "forest of skis stretching from the station gate 
away back to Jean Talon Street." One does not hear of ski 
"specials" today. 


Montreal West & McGill Groups - The Montreal West High School 
Ski Club for five seasons has spent the Christmas holiday per- 


iod at the Lodge. The average number for the party has been 5. 


-h- 


The McGill School of Physical Education has held its Ski 
School at the Lodge for four years. When the School Direct- 
ress enquired about the Lodge, she said, "We would like ac- 
commodation where the bar is not the centre of entertainment 
hours." 


The Autoroute has made a difference in the skiing habits of 
the occasional skier. More of these occasional skiers ski 
one day only . . . and return home. This is especially true 
when skiing conditions are not the best. If is a fact, too, 
that skiers with cars ski at one hill one day or weekend, and 
somewhere else the next. 


The rope tows af Mt. Christie will be replaced by a T-Bar or 
Chair Liff shortly. The Autoroute will be extended through 
St, Sauveur and be within fhree miles of Christievitte. 


House and Shack Owners in the Laurentians have no difficulty 
renting their buildings for the skiing season. tn the im- 
mediate neighbourhood of the Lodge, the houses are all rented 
by the end of October. Hereabouts the better houses are 

taken by families who pay $500 - $600 for the season. "Shacks" 
rent at $350 - $400. One shack which rented last winter had 

no inside foilet; one in St, Sauveur, which had no hot water 
tank, rented to six girls at $500. One shack near the Lodge 
with no water supply at all has been rented for this season. 


A Group (including several Otoreke campers) has been organ- 
ized to weekend at different areas this winter. Plans catl 
for visits to Jay Peak, Mt. Washington, Stowe, Mt. Tremblant, 
etc. Tremblant is the only area in Canada mentioned in their 
list of areas. To the question, "Why not spend a weekend at 
the 'Y' Lodge?" the answer was, "What with rope tows!" 


The Friendly Home, which rented the house from John Elder for 
the summer in the years before we took over, continues to 
rent from us. The rent is $400... the same as paid to 

Mr. Elder.
